blocks.text: This chapter records the pivotal Davidic covenant. David, dwelling in his cedar palace while the ark remains under curtains, proposes to Nathan that he should build a permanent temple. But God, through Nathan, redirects David's intention. Rather than David building for God, God promises to build for David: his descendants will construct the temple, and God will establish David's dynasty and throne forever. This covenant transforms the narrative from David's initiative into God's sovereign plan for both the kingdom and the temple.
